title: Fate Marable learns calliope from Charlie Mills
summary: Charlie Mills trains Fate Marable, who leads the New Orleans boat orchestra around 1920 and first employs Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: The violin player? The violin player, yeah. The violin player was Charlie Hershoff from Dora, Illinois. And the drummer was, the name was Little. The first name I don't know. That was the three, that was the combination of piano, violin and drums. That was the first combination. And later on, of course, went to the larger orchestras. How long was Melton on the band? And then he broke in another piano player by the name of Fate Merrill, Fate Merrill from Patooga, Kentucky, to play the clap. His fellow Charlie Mills was the best clapboard player we ever had. He was the original. We had clapboard those days. He broke in Fate Merrill who played the clap. This was done on the trips down the river and would stop between towns and then he practiced in two or three hours. He was a little disturbed the public. I guess that would wake a whole town up. Well, this fellow Fate Merrill then became a very fine piano player and always had the orchestra on the boat and then on and worked with all the rest of his life. He had the orchestra in New Orleans called the Cotton Fingers. He played in New Orleans here mostly in the heyday. It was around 1920. And he was the first fellow to employ William Armstrong. Fate Merrill with him.
But the excursion boats had the 8-9 piece bands, which we still have now.
